assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new measurement instrument that opened a door: optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength trapping idea, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have redefined what can be measured, from relativistic redshift across millimetres to searches for variation of constants and a future redefinition of the second. This is an invention with a clear, original experiment and direct benefit to metrology and fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and led the first strontium lattice clock demonstrations; Jun Ye brought the system to the highest accuracy and stability and drove the many-body and gravitational-redshift applications. A two-person prize is clean and fits the credited names. Other groups contributed to specific atoms and techniques, which I cannot fully adjudicate from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide with agreeing frequency ratios over more than two decades. The performance record is stable, and recognition is timely, though the redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Katori's original proposal versus Ye's later accuracy milestones is a matter for the historical record.
Whether the committee prefers to fold this together with related frequency-comb and ion-clock work already recognised in earlier prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope and opened neutrino astronomy with the 2013 detection of a high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, followed by the TXS 0506+056 blazar association and Galactic-plane neutrinos. This is exactly a new window onto phenomena that could not be seen before, and it is experimentally verified.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and collaboration; Karle was central to the detector construction and the optical-module and ice-calibration work. The collaboration is large, so any two- or three-person configuration is a compromise. I choose the two names with the clearest leadership of the original idea and realisation, but I would want the record on AMANDA to IceCube examined carefully.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and the first source associations are reasonably strong, though individual source identification is still developing. Recognition is timely, since the discovery is robust even if source physics remains open.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution and the role of Shigeru Yoshida and other leaders in the AMANDA and IceCube history.
Source associations such as TXS 0506+056 are only moderate statistical significance; the origin of most of the flux is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in 1995 was the original experiment that made magnetic tunnel junctions practical, and it underlies hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The effect was measured, understood and rapidly turned into technology that benefits society at a very large scale.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in amorphous-aluminium-oxide junctions in 1995; this is the original experiment. Parkin's later contribution on MgO-based junctions with giant TMR was an important improvement but, in the spirit of crediting the original experiment rather than the later better one, I leave him out, while recognising that the committee may disagree. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature precursor is not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of independent confirmation and commercial deployment. The slight timing issue is that the 2007 prize recognised giant magnetoresistance in the same technological family.
uncertainties: Possible view that this is incremental relative to the GMR prize.
Whether Parkin's MgO work should be credited as a separate and decisive advance.
Julliere's earlier observation sits outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nd-Fe-B is the strongest commercial permanent magnet and underpins wind turbines, electric motors, hard-disk actuators and consumer electronics. As a materials person I value that the discovery combined a new compound with a processing route that made it useful; the impact on energy technology is large and undeniable.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo Special Metals, sintered route) and Croat (General Motors, melt-spun route) announced the compound essentially simultaneously and independently in 1983-84, so a two-person prize is natural. The question of who did the original discovery is a real historical issue, and I would want the primary record checked before committing.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with forty years of industrial use and independent verification. Recognition, if anything, is overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards a materials and engineering discovery as physics-prize scope.
Priority dispute and patent history between the two groups, and the role of coworkers not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent manipulation of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond at room temperature opened a door to nanoscale quantum sensing of magnetic fields, temperature and electric fields, including in biological settings. It is an experimental tool that lets us see things not visible before, with wide use in materials characterisation.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and colleagues demonstrated optical detection of single NV centres in 1997 and Jelezko and Wrachtrup showed coherent control in 2004; those are the original experiments. Lukin contributed important proposals and sensing demonstrations, but I judge the decisive experimental credit to lie with the first two. Early NV optical-spectroscopy work by other groups is not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups and widely adopted. Applications continue to evolve and some sensing claims are still developing, but the underlying discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Leaving out Lukin may be contested given the breadth of his role in sensing and quantum-register work.
Overlap with other quantum-technology candidates and uncertain boundary between discovery and engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall state and topological insulators represent a new classification of electronic matter, and the experimental observation of helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells was the decisive verification of a theoretical prediction. It has opened a large field of topological materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theoretical prediction, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation; Molenkamp's group made the original experimental observation in 2007. Xue's group is more associated with the quantum anomalous Hall effect and so a different compound discovery. The supplied names for this entry are Kane, Molenkamp and Xue; I choose the two that I think best match the original prediction and original experiment, noting that the theory credit is genuinely shared and that the late Shoucheng Zhang is not eligible.
assessment.maturity: The quantum spin Hall edge transport has been confirmed in HgTe and later in other systems. Three-dimensional topological insulators have been verified by ARPES from several groups. Mature, with continued but not essential development.
uncertainties: Fair division of theory credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Fu is unresolved and complicates a three-person configuration.
A compound discovery whose quantum anomalous Hall component may warrant separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire gain media and passive mode-locking made reliable femtosecond laser sources routine, and they are the enabling tool behind ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and the attosecond physics the committee honoured in 2023. This is a door-opening instrument invention with a long chain of applications.
assessment.attribution: Moulton demonstrated the Ti:sapphire laser, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking in it, and Keller invented semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors for self-starting passive mode-locking. These are three distinct, original contributions and a three-person configuration is plausible. Keller would also be a woman laureate, which I note without letting it replace the scientific case.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and universally used. Some of the downstream impact has already been recognised in earlier prizes on chirped-pulse amplification, combs and attosecond pulses, which may reduce the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with previously recognised ultrafast work and the exact priority between Kerr-lens and other mode-locking mechanisms.
Whether the committee sees the three contributions as one coherent discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays opened the nanohertz gravitational-wave window, and the 2023 evidence for a stochastic background with Hellings-Downs-like angular correlation is a new observation of the universe made with a distinct instrument, the Galaxy-scale detector. It is also an original experiment in the sense of timing precision and array design.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, and others), so it is hard to name three people without arbitrary choices. McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester respectively represent the North American, European and Australian efforts, which is a reasonable geographic balance but not clearly the decisive individuals. The credit structure is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Premature. The evidence is at roughly the three to four sigma level, the source of the signal (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) is not settled, and independent confirmation with further data releases is still pending.
uncertainties: Statistical significance below discovery level and no single-source detection yet.
Interpretation of the background amplitude and spectrum is unsettled.
Attribution among three large collaborations and the pioneers of precision pulsar timing is unresolved.
